as_read: Raises blood NAD+ reliably, but clinical primary outcomes are null in cognition and long-COVID, worse than placebo in Parkinson disease, and positive in one peripheral artery disease trial.

studies_to_add.primary_endpoint: change in total MDS-UPDRS at week 52
studies_to_add.quote: Among patients with early Parkinson disease, nicotinamide riboside treatment for 52 weeks did not improve clinical outcomes and was associated with worse clinical outcomes than placebo.
There were no improvements in cognitive function (primary outcome), total CBF, or blood pressure (secondary outcomes).
In this work, NR meaningfully improved 6-min walk, and resveratrol did not add benefit to NR alone in PAD.

rejection.search: "nicotinamide riboside hydrogen malate" OR "NR hydrogen malate" OR NRHM[Title/Abstract] OR NiaCel[Title/Abstract] OR "riboside malate" OR "hydrogen malate": count 140, first 25 reviewed by title; hits were mostly India's National Rural Health Mission and plant or chemistry papers; the only salt paper seen is 34066468, a chemistry paper by title and snippet, with no human trial

clinician_items: 42848371: nicotinamide riboside 1000 mg/day for 52 weeks in early Parkinson disease: MDS-UPDRS worsened versus placebo, difference 2.72 points, P = .02; non-motor symptoms worse, P = .009. Serious adverse events 8.3% versus 14.1% on placebo.
37994989: walking speed improved on placebo but not nicotinamide riboside at 1 g/day; the authors read the placebo change as a practice effect.
stored_rating_note: positive_moderate rests on blood NAD+ alone (31278280, 27721479), a surrogate. The clinical primaries read here don't support moderate; mixed fits better. 27721479 is pharmacokinetics plus a mouse arm, not an efficacy trial.
